title: Define Agent runtime data model
purpose: Replace lifecycle skeleton types with a versioned runtime data model that can represent real Agent plans and runs.
scope: Define IntentCtx with actor, trust boundary, source, current working scope, and requested outcome.
Define PlanSpec with plan_id, planner version, steps, dependencies, success criteria, risk hints, rollback requirements, and model evidence metadata.
Define PlanStep with semantic tool call, dependency list, preconditions, expected observations, verification rule, approval requirement, and retry budget.
Define PlanRun with run_id, frozen_plan_hash, state, current step cursor, approval state, observation references, memory references, and recovery marker.
Define Observation with source, trust label, normalized result, summary, redaction status, and policy-relevant flags.
Add deterministic JSON serialization suitable for audit and persisted run-state snapshots.
deliverables: crates/agentd/src/agent_core.rs or equivalent runtime model module
Unit tests for PlanSpec and PlanRun serialization
acceptance_criteria: A service recovery intent can be represented as a PlanSpec without executing any tool.
PlanSpec includes enough metadata to re-evaluate risk after restart.
PlanRun can be serialized and loaded without losing state.
Risk hints are represented as hints, not authoritative decisions.
Secret values cannot be stored in IntentCtx, PlanSpec, PlanRun, or Observation fields.
verification: Snapshot-test a service recovery PlanSpec JSON.
Attempt to construct a model containing password/token-like values and confirm redaction or rejection.
Confirm no side-effect audit events are emitted by model construction.
risk_notes: If PlanSpec is too weak, downstream runtime code will fall back to ad hoc workflow-specific state.
